source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension / ASPIRE Project (IFAD-funded) - "Climate Resilient Banana Growing Technique" (ផលិតកម្មដំណាំចេកដែលធន់ទៅនឹងការប្រែប្រួលអាកាសធាតុ), November 2018
text:
Harvest signs mirror standard banana practice: bunches are cut once the fruit's angular ridges have rounded out and filled in, generally corresponding to about 75-80% maturity rather than full ripeness on the plant, since fruit cut too green fails to ripen properly and fruit left to ripen fully on the stem is more prone to damage and pest attack before harvest.

After cutting, bunches are handled carefully to avoid bruising during transport, and post-harvest ripening is generally done off the plant in a shaded, covered space that traps the fruit's own ethylene to bring on even ripening over a few days.
